breakfast.name: Potica (Nut Roll)
ingredients: Dough: flour, yeast, milk, butter, eggs
Filling: ground walnuts, sugar, honey, cream, rum, cinnamon
instructions: Make rich yeast dough, rise
Roll very thin on tablecloth
Spread walnut filling
Roll up tightly using the cloth
Coil into round pan
Bake at 175°C 60 min
breakfast.description: Slovenia's iconic rolled sweet bread — walnut-filled, coiled, and baked.

breakfast.name: Žganci (Buckwheat Spoonbread)
instructions: Boil water with salt
Add buckwheat flour, do not stir
When cooked, break into chunks with fork
Toss with cracklings

breakfast.name: Zganci (Buckwheat Porridge)
instructions: Zganci are the Slovenian buckwheat groats -- an ancient breakfast food
Buckwheat flour cooked in boiling salted water until it forms crumbly clumps
Stirred with a wooden spoon -- the clumps are deliberately formed
Finished with hot lard or oil drizzled over
The lard sizzles on the buckwheat -- the sound and smell are the experience
Eaten with sour cream or milk poured over
Buckwheat is indigenous to Central Asia but found its home in Slovenia
breakfast.description: Slovenian buckwheat porridge -- buckwheat flour cooked in salted water into crumbly clumps (deliberately, not smooth), finished with hot drizzled lard that sizzles on contact, served with sour cream or milk. An ancient Slovenian breakfast.

breakfast.name: Potica (Walnut Roll) -- Morning Slice
ingredients: Potica (leftover from the holiday loaf -- eaten cold for breakfast)
instructions: Potica is the Slovenian rolled pastry -- the symbol of Slovenian food
Made for Easter, Christmas, and every celebration
Leftover potica is eaten cold for breakfast the next day
The morning-after slice: cold, dense, walnut-sweet
Slovenians abroad consider potica the taste of home
breakfast.description: Slovenian morning potica slice -- cold leftover walnut roll (the Slovenian celebration pastry) eaten for breakfast. Potica is the symbol of Slovenian food: made for Easter, Christmas, and celebrations. Cold the next morning, it is the taste of home for Slovenians abroad.

lunch.name: Jota (Bean and Sauerkraut Soup)
instructions: Cook beans until nearly tender
Add sauerkraut, potatoes, smoked meat
Simmer 45 min
Add garlic
Drizzle with olive oil to serve
lunch.description: Hearty bean and sauerkraut soup — Slovenian soul food.

lunch.name: Štruklji (Rolled Dumplings)
ingredients: Filling: cottage cheese, tarragon (or walnut, apple)
instructions: Stretch dough thin on cloth
Spread filling
Roll up, wrap in cloth
Boil or steam 30 min
Slice, top with buttered breadcrumbs
lunch.description: Rolled stuffed dumplings — savory or sweet.

lunch.name: Idrijski Zlikrofi (Idrija Ravioli)
ingredients: Potato filling: boiled potato, lard, onion, marjoram, chives
instructions: Idrijski zlikrofi are the Slovenian ravioli -- EU-protected designation
Named after Idrija, a town in western Slovenia (historically famous for mercury mining)
The pocket shape: a distinctive square with a pinched top -- like a little hat
The filling: potato with lard, onion, and marjoram
Boiled and served with butter and breadcrumbs
Idrija is also famous for bobbin lace -- and for zlikrofi
lunch.description: Slovenian Idrija ravioli -- EU-protected designation, from the mercury-mining town of Idrija. Distinctive square pasta pockets with a pinched top, filled with potato, lard, onion, and marjoram, boiled and served with butter and breadcrumbs.

lunch.name: Bograch (Prekmurje Goulash)
ingredients: Beef, pork, and game (the Prekmurje three-meat version)
instructions: Bograch is the Slovenian Prekmurje goulash -- a variation of Hungarian goulash
Prekmurje is the easternmost Slovenian region -- heavily Hungarian-influenced
Three meats: beef, pork, and traditionally also game
Three paprikas: sweet, hot, and smoked -- the Prekmurje signature
Cooked in a bograch (a specific copper pot) over open fire
The bograch pot gives the dish its name
lunch.description: Slovenian Prekmurje three-meat goulash -- beef, pork, and game braised with three types of paprika (sweet, hot, smoked), potato, and red wine in a copper bograch pot over open fire. Prekmurje borders Hungary and the dish reflects that cultural overlap.

lunch.name: Rika (Slovenian Bean Soup)
instructions: Rika is the Slovenian bean soup
Similar to Friulian and Italian bean soups -- the border region influence
Beans cooked with smoked pork
Marjoram: the essential Slovenian herb
Savory (cajeput): another Slovenian herb
lunch.description: Slovenian bean soup -- borlotti beans with smoked pork, carrot, and celery, seasoned with marjoram and savory (the essential Slovenian herbs). Reflects the influence of neighboring Friuli and Austria. Thick and comforting.

dinner.name: Kraški Pršut with Teran
instructions: Slice prosciutto thin
Serve with bread and olives
Pair with a glass of Teran
dinner.description: Karst-region dry-cured ham — a Slovenian treasure.

dinner.name: Ričet (Barley Stew)
instructions: Cook barley and beans
Add smoked pork, vegetables
Simmer 45 min until thick
dinner.description: Thick barley and bean stew with smoked pork.

dinner.name: Truklji (Sweet Cottage Cheese Rolls)
ingredients: Sweet cottage cheese (tvaroh + sugar + eggs + vanilla + raisins)
instructions: Strukli are the Slovenian sweet filled pasta rolls
The name: structure (to roll) -- the dough is rolled around the filling
The filling: sweet cottage cheese with raisins and vanilla
Boiled or baked
Served with sour cream or melted butter
Shared with Croatia -- the Croatian variant is served as a side dish too
dinner.description: Slovenian sweet cottage cheese pasta rolls -- strudel dough filled with sweet tvaroh (cottage cheese, raisins, vanilla), rolled, boiled or baked, served with sour cream. The name means rolled. Shared with Croatia.

dinner.name: Ribja Postna Jed (Lenten Fish Dish)
ingredients: Freshwater fish: trout, carp, pike (from Slovenian rivers and lakes)
instructions: Slovenian freshwater fish: the rivers and lakes of Slovenia are clean and full of trout
The Soca River: famous for marble trout (Salmo marmoratus) -- a native Slovenian fish
Poached in white wine court-bouillon
Served with parsley and the cooking liquid
The Lenten fish dish: Catholic tradition of fish on Fridays
dinner.description: Slovenian freshwater fish -- trout or carp from clean Slovenian rivers (the Soca is famous for marble trout, a native species) poached in white wine court-bouillon with vegetables and herbs. Catholic Lenten tradition of Friday fish dishes.

dinner.name: Prekmurska Gibanica (Prekmurje Layered Cake)
ingredients: Four fillings: poppy seed, cottage cheese, walnut, apple
instructions: Prekmurska gibanica is the Slovenian multi-layer pastry -- EU-protected
Four fillings in repeating layers: poppy seed, cottage cheese, walnut, apple
Each layer is distinct -- the cross-section shows four colors
The word gibanica means to move or fold -- referring to the layering
Prekmurje: the easternmost Slovenian region where this originated
Now considered a national Slovenian treasure
dinner.description: Slovenian EU-protected layered pastry -- four alternating fillings (poppy seed, cottage cheese, walnut, apple) in repeated layers of pastry, revealing four-color cross-section when cut. Gibanica means to fold. From Prekmurje, now a national Slovenian symbol.

snacks.name: Ajdovi Žganci (Buckwheat)
instructions: Pour flour into boiling water
Cook without stirring
Break into chunks with fork
Serve with cracklings
snacks.description: Chunky buckwheat — eaten as snack or side.

snacks.name: Slovenian Honey (Med)
ingredients: Slovenian honey (any variety: acacia, linden, chestnut, forest honey)
instructions: Slovenia has one of the highest densities of beehives in the world
The Carniolan bee (Apis mellifera carnica) is the native Slovenian bee -- exported worldwide
Slovenian honey is among the most prized in Europe
Varieties: acacia (light, mild), linden (aromatic), chestnut (bitter, dark), forest (complex)
Eaten on bread, in tea, or directly from the spoon
snacks.description: Slovenian single-origin honey -- from the Carniolan bee (native Slovenian bee, exported worldwide). Slovenia has among the highest beehive densities in Europe. Varieties: acacia (light), linden (aromatic), chestnut (dark, bitter), forest (complex). Eaten on bread or in tea.

snacks.name: Bujta Repa (Turnip and Millet)
ingredients: Turnips (fermented -- similar to sauerkraut but turnip)
instructions: Bujta repa is the Prekmurje fermented turnip dish
Turnips are fermented in the same way as sauerkraut
Cooked with millet and smoked pork
A thick, porridge-like stew
Deeply traditional Slovenian peasant food from the Prekmurje region
snacks.description: Slovenian fermented turnip porridge -- fermented turnips (prepared like sauerkraut) cooked with millet and smoked pork ribs into a thick stew. Prekmurje traditional peasant food.

snacks.name: Popcorn Strudel Chips
instructions: Leftover strudel dough scraps are brushed with butter and baked or fried
Dusted with cinnamon sugar
A resourceful use of strudel dough trimmings
snacks.description: Slovenian strudel dough scraps -- thin leftover strudel dough brushed with butter, baked until crispy, dusted with cinnamon sugar. A resourceful use of trimmings.

desserts.name: Prekmurska Gibanica (Layered Cake)
ingredients: Fillings: cottage cheese, walnuts, apples, poppy seeds
instructions: Layer filo with each filling alternately
Top with cream mixture
Bake at 180°C 60 min
Cool, dust with sugar
desserts.description: Prekmurje layered pastry — four fillings, nine layers.

desserts.name: Potica (Walnut Roll)
ingredients: Yeast dough (rich -- egg, butter, milk, sugar)
Walnut filling: ground walnuts, honey, warm milk, cinnamon, rum
instructions: Potica is the Slovenian national pastry -- the most important Slovenian sweet
A rolled yeast dough pastry with walnut filling
The word potica: from potice (to roll) -- the dough is rolled very thin
The walnut filling: ground walnuts, honey, warm milk, cinnamon, and rum
The dough is rolled out, filled, and rolled up into a log
Baked in a round mold or straight as a log
Made for Easter, Christmas, and every celebration
Dozens of regional variations: walnut, poppy seed, tarragon, cottage cheese
desserts.description: Slovenian national celebration pastry -- rich yeast dough rolled very thin and filled with ground walnut-honey-cinnamon-rum filling, rolled into a log and baked. Dozens of regional variations (poppy seed, tarragon, cottage cheese). Made for Easter and Christmas. The Slovenian taste of home.

desserts.name: Krofe (Slovenian Doughnuts)
ingredients: Yeast dough (enriched with eggs and butter)
instructions: Krofe are the Slovenian doughnuts -- filled with plum jam
The plum jam: from Slovenian plum orchards
The dough is enriched and light
Fried until golden and hollow
Filled with plum jam via piping bag
Dusted with icing sugar
Eaten at carnival time (pustovanje -- the Slovenian carnival season)
desserts.description: Slovenian plum jam doughnuts -- enriched yeast dough fried until golden and hollow, filled with plum jam (from Slovenian plum orchards), dusted with icing sugar. Eaten at pustovanje (Slovenian carnival season).

drinks.name: Teran Wine
instructions: Serve at room temperature
Pair with pršut and cheese
drinks.description: Deep red wine from Slovenia's iron-rich Karst soil.

drinks.name: Borovničke (Blueberry Schnapps)
instructions: Serve chilled as digestif

drinks.name: Vipava Wine (Orange Wine)
ingredients: Ribolla Gialla or Pinot Grigio (white grapes -- Vipava Valley)
instructions: Vipava Valley is one of the oldest wine regions in Europe
The orange wine movement: Slovenia is one of its global centers
Orange wine: white grapes fermented with the skins on -- like a red wine but white grapes
The skin contact gives tannin, color (orange-amber), and complexity
Stanko Radikon and Josko Gravner (Friulian side): the pioneers of modern orange wine
Slovenian Vipava and Karst: the traditional home of skin-contact white wine
drinks.description: Slovenian Vipava Valley orange wine -- white grapes (Ribolla Gialla, Pinot Grigio) fermented with skin contact for amber color and tannin. Slovenia is a global center of the orange wine movement. The Karst and Vipava regions have made skin-contact whites for generations before the trend.
